A long-track tornado path was found from Wallace to Potters Hill. It should be noted that the tornado may have briefly lifted up at times, and may have been an inconstant path especially near Beulaville toward Potters Hill. The most consistent, concentrated damage was found from west of Wallace, northeast to just west of Chinquapin. At the peak, radar indicated debris lofted as high as at least 12,000 ft, but potentially as high as 16,000 ft.

Storm survey found evidence of an EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 115 to 125 mph. The tornado was estimated to be 150 yards wide and 24.43 miles long. Several reports of storm damage including 18 wheeler flipped, cars lifted and dropped, roof damage, power outages and trees down around the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road.

The start of the Bonnie Doone tornado path based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 115 mph (EF-2) occurred on a short quarter-mile section between the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road while otherwise producing EF-0 to EF-1 damage along a discontinuous path for nearly 5.5 miles.

The start of the Linden, NC tornado based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 105 mph (EF-1) occurred along Hungry Creek Drive where several windows were blown out of a residence. The tornado tracked along a nearly continuous path for almost 1.25 miles.
NWS Storm Survey confirmed a brief EF-0 Tornado that crossed US421 between Matthews Rd and Willard Rd. Path length 0.18 miles, width 30 yards. Time on ground approx 1 minute.
